Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the CloudForge Inc. Q2 FY2025 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. To ask a question, please press star then one on your touchtone phone. To withdraw your question, press star then two. Please be advised that today's call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Operator. Good afternoon, everyone, and welcome to CloudForge Inc.'s Q2 FY2025 earnings call. Joining me today are Sarah Chen, CEO; Mike Patel, CFO; Dr. Lena Novak, CTO; Raj Singh, Chief Revenue Officer; Emily Torres, Chief Product Officer; and Jordan Lee, Chief Marketing Officer.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that this call contains forward-looking statements. Actual results may differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Sarah Chen.

Sarah Chen:
Thank you, Alex, and good afternoon, everyone. I'm pleased to report on CloudForge Inc.'s performance for Q2 FY2025. We achieved significant milestones this quarter, driven by strong demand for our ForgeAI Pro platform and continued execution of our strategic initiatives.

Our focus this quarter was on seven key areas: average contract value, or ACV; operating margin; next quarter ARR guidance; NRR performance; ARR growth year-over-year and quarter-over-quarter; churn analysis; and Rule of 40.

Mike will provide the details on these shortly, but overall, these metrics highlight the durability of our land-and-expand model, the power of our AI innovations, and our commitment to profitable growth. We are confident in our ability to continue this momentum and deliver long-term value to our shareholders.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Mike Patel to discuss the financials in more detail.

Mike Patel:
Thank you, Sarah. As Sarah mentioned, we had a strong quarter. Revenue for the quarter was $285 million, representing a 35% increase year-over-year. Our gross margin was 82%, and non-GAAP operating income was $79.8 million, reflecting a 28% operating margin.

We continue to invest in research and development to drive innovation and expand our product offerings. Our cash position remains strong at $450 million, providing us with the flexibility to pursue strategic acquisitions and other growth opportunities.

Let me dive deeper into the seven key areas Sarah highlighted, starting with average contract value, or ACV. ACV came in at $52,300 for the quarter, up 18% year-over-year from $44,300 in Q2 FY2024 and up 5% quarter-over-quarter from $49,800 in Q1 FY2025. This is the sixth straight quarter of double-digit year-over-year ACV growth, which really demonstrates the strength of our land-and-expand approach and the pricing power we're commanding with our AI-powered collaboration and analytics platform.

Just to clarify, ACV is the annualized value of new and expansion contracts divided by the number of customers added in the period. Stripping out one-offs like professional services, our core SaaS ACV shows clear wallet share gains. Breaking it down, enterprise momentum was a big driver—deals over $100K ARR averaged $185,000, up 28% year-over-year and now 42% of our new ACV mix, compared to 35% last year. This comes from multi-year commitments, with 65% of new enterprise customers signing three-year deals at an average of 2.8 years. For instance, our hyperscaler partnership with AWS bundles our GenAI Analytics Engine—essentially Tableau combined with ChatGPT for real-time predictive insights—with their EC2 infrastructure. A Fortune 50 retailer expanded from a $75K pilot to $450K ACV by adding our Workforce Intelligence module, which uses large language models for dynamic workflow automation. This is similar to Salesforce's Einstein expansions or Workday's AI HCM upsells.

In the mid-market segment, $25K to $100K ACV, we saw 12% year-over-year growth to $48,500 average. Usage-based pricing tiers we introduced last year boosted effective ACV by 8% via overages on API calls and storage. SMB ACV was steady at $12,200, but conversions from freemium to paid rose 22% due to self-serve portal improvements.

Regionally, North America, 72% of new ACV, averaged $55,400, up 20% year-over-year, thanks to financial services and healthcare verticals embracing our compliance modules under SEC cybersecurity rules and HIPAA. EMEA, 18% of mix, hit $48,900, up 15%, with GDPR-aligned data sovereignty features lifting ACV in DACH enterprises, much like Snowflake's private instances. APAC, 10%, reached $42,700, up 14%, led by Japan and Australia, though we're cautious on China data localization, keeping it below 2% of bookings.

These trends stem from product-led growth with AI stickiness—our ForgeAI Pro launch drove 35% of expansion revenue, lifting existing ACV by 12% on average. We've shifted go-to-market toward high-ACV deals via our Strategic Account program, cutting sales cycles 15% and boosting win rates to 38%. Pricing discipline with annual true-ups added 4% without impacting churn, which is 4.2% gross dollar. For Q3, we expect ACV of $54,000 to $56,000, or 17-20% year-over-year growth, as we ramp Microsoft Copilot co-sells and enter manufacturing with IoT analytics. This supports our $850 million FY2025 ARR guidance, up 25% year-over-year.

Next, operating margin. Our non-GAAP operating margin hit 28% this quarter, a 600 basis point expansion year-over-year from 22% and 200 basis points better sequentially from Q1's 26%. This is our eighth consecutive quarter of expansion as we scale past $1 billion ARR—now at $1.15 billion, up 32% year-over-year.

Revenue growth outpaced expense growth 3:1, with NRR at 118% from upsells into CloudForge Analytics Pro, which grew 45% in adoption. New logo ACV rose 15% to $125K as enterprises bundled products like Adobe's Experience Cloud. Gross margin improved 150 basis points year-over-year to 82% via AWS Graviton compute savings of 22% and Snowflake data integrations supporting 95% gross retention.

OpEx leverage was key: sales and marketing down to 35% of revenue from 42%, a 700 basis point gain, as product-led growth hit 40% of net new ARR, CAC payback to 14 months from 18, and CAC to $8,500. Inbound leads and AI attribution cut inefficient spend 15%, sales productivity up 25%. R&D steady at 18%, 40% to AI like ForgeAI Agent, boosting NRR 12 points and keeping us in Gartner's Leaders quadrant. G&A to 6% from 7.5% via headcount discipline and automation savings.

Broad-based regionally: U.S. 60% of revenue at 30% margins from AWS/Azure co-sells; EMEA 25% at 26% from GDPR AI; APAC 15% to 18% with Japan wins. This reflects sustainable leverage, with cross-sell at 2.8 products per customer. We expect 30%+ by year-end, with upside from AI pricing like ServiceNow.

Turning to next quarter ARR guidance for Q3. We're guiding to ending ARR of $1.23 billion to $1.26 billion, or 7% to 9.5% sequential growth, $18 million to $24 million net adds, and 38% to 42% year-over-year—well ahead of peers like Snowflake guiding mid-20s.

Core retention: NRR 116-120%, expansions $12-15 million from AI CodeGen at 40% attach. New logos $8-10 million, enterprise pipeline $400 million coverage from FedRAMP wins. North America 75% of ARR at 8-10% growth via AWS Bedrock; EMEA 15% at 10-12%; APAC 10% at 4-6%. Q3 roadmap includes v4.2 Pipeline with agentic AI and zero-trust security, 25% faster builds, 65% POC-to-close. R&D to 22%. Resilient to 5% contraction risk, elite 14-month CAC payback. Upside from AI and M&A. Rule of 50 at 85.

On NRR performance: We delivered 118% NRR, up from 115% last quarter and 110% year-over-year. Gross retention 93%, up 100 basis points; dollar churn 4.1% from 4.8%, logo churn 2.2% from fintech startups, offset by AI Health Score flagging risks 45 days early for 75% uplift.

Contraction 2.9%, down 50 basis points, via usage caps like Snowflake's, under 1.5% in enterprise. Expansion 25% or $45 million from ForgeAI Insights at 40% attach and Kubernetes observability, integrated with Bedrock/OpenAI. North America 122%, EMEA 116%, APAC 108%. Customer success model boosted expansion 15%; expect 117-120% ahead with ForgeAI Enterprise, targeting $2.5 billion ARR by FY26.

ARR growth: Ending ARR $1.15 billion, 32% year-over-year from prior, 7.5% quarter-over-quarter exceeding guidance. New logos $28 million from 320 customers, ForgeAI deals 25% larger; expansions $18 million, 60% of adds; churn/contraction $14 million, 98% gross retention. North America 75% up 31% YoY/8% QoQ; EMEA 42%/6%; APAC 18%/9%. AI 22% of ARR, 150% NRR in adopters; platform cross-sell 65%; GTM efficiency with 11-month CAC. Q4 guide $1.18-1.19 billion.

Churn analysis: Gross dollar retention 112%, NRR 118% from 28% expansions. Logo churn 7.2% annualized, down 120 basis points; dollar 5.9%, beating medians. Reasons: macro 32% voluntary from SMB budgets; competition 29% from Teams/Slack/HubSpot; product friction 39% onboarding/support. North America 6.8%, EMEA 9.4%, APAC 6.2%, LatAm 11.2%.

Mitigations: ChurnGuard ML scores save 42% ($14M ARR), 1:75 CSM ratio, 4,200 interventions. Nexlify AI Retention Suite 62% adoption, cuts early churn 31%; Instant Value Packs to 27-day onboarding; pay-per-active-user retains 91%. EMEA GDPR module stems 65% exits. Guide sub-7% churn, 120% NRR.

Finally, Rule of 40: Score of 63, 35% revenue growth +28% EBITDA margin, up from 40% prior, sixth straight above 40. Revenue $285 million +35%, ARR $1.15 billion +37%. Margin from 82% OpEx leverage, CAC <14 months, NRR 118% from GenAI Suite 40% attach. North America 62% +32%; EMEA +48%; APAC +42%. R&D 14% to security/edge. FCF 9%, Q3 48-50 score.

We are updating our full-year guidance to reflect our strong performance, now expecting ARR around $1.3 billion.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Dr. Lena Novak for a technology update.

Dr. Lena Novak:
Thank you, Mike. This quarter, we made significant progress in advancing our AI capabilities and further integrating them into our core platform. We are seeing strong adoption of our new AI-powered features, which are driving increased user engagement and improved customer outcomes. We've also focused on enhancing our platform's security and scalability to meet the growing demands of our enterprise customers.

And now Emily Torres will provide an update on the product roadmap.

Emily Torres:
Thank you, Lena. We have been focusing on the user experience of our products and are excited to announce the launch of ForgeAI Agent. This new feature significantly improves deployment automation and predictive analytics. We are seeing strong adoption of this feature which aligns with our product strategy.

Jordan Lee:
Thank you, Emily. This quarter our focus was on increasing our brand awareness and lead generation through targeted digital campaigns and strategic partnerships. We saw a 25% increase in website traffic and a 35% increase in qualified leads, demonstrating the effectiveness of our marketing initiatives.

Now, I'll turn the call back to the operator for Q&A.

Operator:
Thank you. To ask a question, please press star then one. Our first question comes from Ben Smith with Goldman Sachs.

Ben Smith:
Hi, good afternoon. Can you discuss the impact of ForgeAI on your overall growth, what kind of attach rates are you seeing, how it compares to your initial expectations, and what's the competitive landscape like?

Raj Singh:
Thanks, Ben. ForgeAI has been a game-changer, contributing over 30% to our net new ARR this quarter through rapid upsells and new logos. Attach rates are hitting 42% on existing customers, exceeding our initial 30% target as enterprises bundle it with core DevOps modules for end-to-end AI workflows. Compared to expectations, we're ahead by 20% in adoption velocity, thanks to seamless integrations. Competitively, we're gaining share from legacy players like Jenkins by offering agentic AI that's 30% faster, positioning us strongly against GitLab Duo and Harness in the AIOps space.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Chen with Morgan Stanley.

Lisa Chen:
What are your plans for international expansion, specifically in the APAC region, what are your key target markets, and what are your expected ROI from these investments?

Sarah Chen:
Great question, Lisa. International remains a priority, with APAC targeted for 20% of FY2026 ARR. Plans include doubling our Tokyo data center capacity and launching sovereign cloud options in Australia and India. Key markets are Japan telcos and public sector, plus Singaporean enterprises. We expect ROI in 12-18 months, with CAC payback under 16 months based on Q2 pilots yielding 2x NRR, insulated by multi-year deals.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Park with JPMorgan.

David Park:
How are you managing churn in the current economic environment, what's the trend you are seeing in NRR, what are your strategies to improve customer retention, and what's the impact of pricing changes on churn?

Mike Patel:
Thanks, David. Churn management is proactive—we're at 4.1% dollar churn, down sequentially, via AI-driven risk scoring and CS interventions saving 42% of at-risk ARR. NRR trending 118%, stable with expansions offsetting macro pressures. Retention strategies include ChurnGuard dashboards, Instant Value Packs cutting onboarding 35%, and pay-per-active pilots boosting renewals 91%. Pricing changes like usage tiers have zero negative churn impact, actually lifting expansions 12% through true-ups.

Operator:
Thank you. I'm showing no further questions at this time. I'd like to turn the call back over to Sarah Chen for closing remarks.

Sarah Chen:
Thank you for joining us today. We are pleased with our progress this quarter and remain committed to delivering strong results for our shareholders. We look forward to speaking with you again on our next earnings call.

Operator:
Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
